item.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's divisive character models may reflect Shigeru Miyamoto's love of puppetry, one Nintendo veteran believes.
item.description:
This week’s Zelda Direct finally revealed gameplay for the Ocarina of Time remake. But while the reveal triggered a wave of nostalgia for the 1998 original N64 game, the remake’s art style divided opinion. The new character designs, in particular for Link, came under particular scrutiny.
Weighing in on the topic on Twitter / X, Nintendo veteran Takaya Imamura suggested the new character models may reflect developer legend Shigeru Miyamoto’s love of puppetry.
“What I felt upon seeing this character model (of Link) is that Miyamoto-san’s love of puppet dramas (ningyogeki) is strongly reflected here too!” Imamura said. His opinion is worth considering — Imamura worked at Nintendo for over 30 years, particularly on the Star Fox and F-Zero series, and of course, was the art director for Ocarina of Time’s sequel, The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask.
It’s important to note that Imamura is just speculating here (as he clarified in a follow-up post) on the inspiration behind the Ocarina of Time remake’s character designs. However, Miyamoto’s love of puppets is well-known, and the use of their aesthetics can be seen across other Nintendo series and promotions. Let’s look at some possible inspirations behind The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s character models.
Aside from Japan’s traditional bunraku puppet theatre, Japanese broadcasters have produced many TV series featuring puppets, particularly in the 1960s and 70s. For example, national broadcaster NHK’s archives under the “ningyogeki” genre category bring up a whole page featuring short clips from puppet TV shows spanning from the 1950s to the present day. Other TV stations got in on the act as well. Japan also imported puppet series including Gerry Anderson’s Thunderbirds, which acquired an enduring fanbase and influence on anime.
Link’s new look seems to be a call back to the whimsy and nostalgia of such TV series (and in keeping with the classic game itself). But some commenters were quick to notice that Ocarina of Time remake’s sharp-nosed, big-eyed characters also bear a strong resemblance to more recent Japanese puppet TV series. Specifically, NHK’s The New Three Musketeers (Shin Sanjushi, 2009-2010), not to mention the 2014 puppet version of Sherlock Holmes. The puppets for The Three Musketeers adaptation were made by legendary Japanese puppet maker Studio Nova, which also made the physical dolls that were used to create Dragon Quest 7 Reimagined’s character models.
Analyzing the new character designs for the Ocarina of Time remake has seen commenters sharing their own comparisons to classic puppet series and movies. The oversized, plastic-looking eyes and prominent facial features have reminded some of 1982 fantasy classic The Dark Crystal (and its more recent Netflix prequel).
Of course, Nintendo fans will have spotted Miyamoto’s fondness for puppets before now. For example, the Star Fox characters strongly resemble The Muppets in style, with actual puppets being used in the TV ad campaign for the series’ very first game back in 1993 (Time Extension).
And who can forget all the puppets used in Nintendo’s 2015 E3 presentation? The game company went all out, teaming up with The Jim Henson company (of The Muppets fame). Miyamoto, then Nintendo America president Reggie Fils-Aimé, and late Nintendo Japan president Satoru Iwata, among others, were all transformed into Muppet-like puppets.
At the time, Fils-Aimé talked to IGN about Miyamoto’s love of puppets. “One of the things that he shared was that in his youth, he used to make puppets," he said. "So that led to a series of brainstorms and it led to our little collaboration with Henson studios and creating the Nintendo muppets. It was a very fun collaboration.”
A remake of such a beloved classic like The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time was always going to please some fans and leave others wanting. What do you think of the new character designs?
Are marionette models a good fit for Hyrule or do the sharp-nosed, doll-like faces put you off? Let us know in the comments.
Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

item.title: IGN exclusively reveals Hour Zero, a new four-part live-action prequel miniseries for Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve starring Josh Holloway and Brandon Routh.
item.description:
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, the latest entry of the long-running flight simulation combat series from Bandai Namco, is hitting PCs and consoles next month. But before players get their hands on the game, IGN can exclusively reveal that a live-action prequel miniseries starring Lost’s Josh Holloway and Superman Returns’ Brandon Routh will be available to stream later this month.
The trailer for Hour Zero, which you can see in the player above, shows Holloway, Routh, and Cobra Kai’s Tamlyn Tomita as “three strangers who survive the opening days of the Republic of Sotoa's invasion of the Federation of Central Usea,” according to the series’ official description.
Holloway stars as “a pilot with nowhere to land,” Routh plays a “doctor who saved his enemy,” and Tomita portrays a “news anchor silenced for telling the truth.” Bandai Namco says the characters’ stories “set the stage for the narrative players will experience in the deep, engaging Campaign Mode in Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve.”
I spoke to Holloway ahead of the show’s launch about jumping into the cockpit and joining the Ace Combat universe. Holloway says that acting in the series reignited his love of gaming.
“When I was younger, I was a gamer,” Holloway says. “Ms. Pac-Man, Centipede, Galaga. I went away from gaming for many, many years, and this has gotten me addicted. It's so real and so visceral. Layering a story onto this game really raises the stakes. After playing the game, I could feel myself in that cockpit because I got to do it in the studio. So now I have that sense memory while I'm playing the game, which is a blast.”
Holloway says that getting to participate in the action scenes of Hour Zero fulfilled one of his lifelong dreams, dating all the way back to before Top Gun was on the big screen.
“God, my first fantasy about being a fighter pilot was [the 1970s World War II fighter pilot TV series] Baa Baa Black Sheep. Remember that? That just tore my imagination up. When I was in high school, I looked into how I could become a fighter pilot. [But] you have to be a fricking math genius for them to let you in the hundred million dollar plane. That dashed my dreams of actually being a fighter pilot. [But I thought,] Aha, I can still be an actor. For me, being a fighter pilot is right up there with being a cowboy.”
Holloway, who appeared in the 2007 game Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars, says that he’s not particularly keen on revisiting performance capture in another video game, but is up for adapting more games for the big screen.
“I'm less interested in being a part of the video game world. [Instead,] I'd like to turn one of those into a movie. I feel like there's room in the Ace Combat world to possibly make a feature. Same thing with cowboy[s]. I do want to do that. I've looked at Red Dead Redemption. It's not just a game anymore. They're like real simulators with real stories.”
Holloway, who’s had the chance to play through Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve ahead of the game’s public release, says there’s one major tip he has for anyone who decides to dive in on October 2.
“Be aggressive,” Holloway says. “If I start to chill out, I got somebody locked on my tail already. So you’ve got to be like, ‘Oh my God, I'm going for it,’ and just hammer down.”
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve will be available in early access for Deluxe Edition holders on September 29 and launch for all players on October 2. The game is available now for preorder on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam.
Michael Peyton is the Senior Editorial Director of Events & Entertainment at IGN, leading entertainment content and coverage of tentpole events including IGN Live, San Diego Comic Con, gamescom, and IGN Fan Fest. He's spent 20 years working in the games and entertainment industry, and his adventures have taken him everywhere from the Oscars to Japan to Buenos Aires, Argentina. Follow him on Bluesky @MichaelPeyton

item.title: We asked the directors about physical media, how they chose the finale's subtitle, and more.
item.description:
Final Fantasy VII Revelation is the finale of Square Enix's ambitious project that began with FFVII Remake in 2020 and continued with FFVII Rebirth in 2024. A full trilogy that retells and remixes the story and world of one of the most beloved video games of all time is a crazy idea on paper, but in less than a year, it will be complete. IGN recently went hands-on with Revelation -- you can read Michael Higham's preview coverage for his in-depth thoughts -- and after playing for roughly two hours for myself, I sat down with two of the creators responsible for bringing this saga to a satisfying conclusion: Director Naoki Hamaguchi and Battle Director Teruki Endo.
I asked the pair (through an interpreter) about how they're keeping the third entry fresh, both with small adjustments to the combat system and new events in areas we already visited in Rebirth. But I was most fascinated to learn about Square Enix's approach to wrapping up this saga: How did they choose a subtitle for this all-important finale? What has this team learned from releasing three AAA RPGs in the span of eight years? And, how does Hamaguchi feel about Revelation releasing on a PlayStation 5 disc in Sony's final year of producing physical games? Read on to learn about all of this and more, including how Fortnite of all things inspired Revelation in one key way.
IGN: Thank you both so much for meeting with me. I appreciate the time. I played about two hours of Final Fantasy VII Revelation yesterday, and I really liked it. And something I'm most interested in is that there are new areas in Revelation, but a lot of it is the same map as Rebirth. I'm curious about the team's process for revisiting old areas and adding interesting content to differentiate them from how they appeared in Rebirth.
Hamaguchi: So I will say that all the various side quests and side contents that are going to be appearing in FFVII Revelation, those are going to be completely new. And with the meteor looming in the sky over the planet, there are a lot of, I guess, seismic shifts that have occurred because of the meteor approaching. So there are various geographical changes that you'll be able to see in the existing areas from Rebirth. So even though they are continuously appearing from various games, it is going to look a little bit different from the previous game.
But in terms of how the actual gameplay and the exploration might feel different from Rebirth is that when we were making Rebirth, the focus was on the open world aspect of the game. So we wanted to introduce a lot of large, vast areas that offered the horizontal width in terms of how big the area is going to look like. With FFVII Revelation, we want to take it a step above. So in addition to the horizontal width, we're now adding a vertical depth that allows players to explore using the Highwind or the Chocobo. So both of these modes of transportation allow you to fly and jump high in the air and things like that. So it does give you a more expanded feel of how the open world is going to look like in the world of the FFVII Remake series. So in that sense, even with the preexisting areas appearing in FFVII Revelation, the way you might approach, the way you might explore, and the way it feels when you explore these areas might feel different from FFVII Rebirth.
IGN: I did like the Highwind a lot, and being able to skydive down into different areas and steer where I landed. It indicates there will be a lot of freedom in how you re-explore areas. And I'm wondering if there were challenges in developing what appears to be a game that's maybe more freeform than Rebirth in how you can tackle objectives.
Hamaguchi: So this kind of ties into the first question that you had, but one of the goals that we had as a development team is to kind of expand as we step into the next installment. So from Remake to Rebirth and from Rebirth to Revelation, we wanted to take a step above. So from the evolution from going from Rebirth and then heading into Revelation was that again, “how can we expand the open world?” And the way we achieved that is to achieve this planetary exploration, the open world map scale where players can just really just explore the entire planet using the Highwind. So taking on that challenge was one of the rather difficult parts of the development for sure.
So the idea of the party parachuting down from the Highwind was something that we had pretty early on in the development of FFVII revelation. When you look at the original release of FFVII, the way it worked was that the Highwind would just land directly onto the ground and the characters would just exit out of the ship. But if we were to do that in this very high fidelity open world, we’d need to think of how the geography would work out in the map. So we needed designed surfaces where it would make sense for the Highwind to be able to smoothly land, if that makes sense. But that wasn't really realistic for us to consider. So that's why we had this parachuting idea. And when you look at other games, specifically like Fortnite, it did seem that players, modern audiences, were pretty familiar or welcome to this idea of characters flying down the air using parachutes. So I thought it would be a fun way to also introduce a seamless transition from the air to the ground. And I think the end result turned out well for us. I'm really happy with how that is in the game.
IGN: As exploration has evolved, combat has evolved in each new entry as well. In Revelation, there's a version of classes, fighting on Chocobos, and other tweaks. How did you decide what elements to stack on the combat system previously established in Remake and evolved in Rebirth?
Endo: We as a team felt that the combat system was in a perfect state with FFVII Rebirth. So while we did think about, “what can we do to add more?”, we couldn't really find any areas that needed to be improved, if that makes sense. I feel like it was in pretty good state already. So because of that, rather than coming up with ideas of how we can change something, it was more about expanding what we already had, because again, we felt that the combat system we had in Rebirth was already really good and in a perfected, complete state. So the idea was more about, “how can we offer more flexibility for customization and freedom to players?” So that's kind of the approach that we had, and how we came with the ideas of the FITS system and the Chocobos engaging in combat.
IGN: Would it be fair to say one of the themes of Revelation from a gameplay perspective is freedom? I think about the Highwind’s exploration, and then what you just said about the combat. Was that kind of a core idea of this game?
Hamaguchi: I think yes, but one of the very big concepts that we had for this game is resolve. So resolve being the core theme of the game, that doesn't only just apply to the story or the characters, it also applies to the overall game experience that the players will have when they play FFVII Revelation. So the idea is that we want the players to make the choice themselves. We're going to offer them a lot of different options and choices and they can choose to control or play as Cloud, but they can also choose to play as the different party members in this game as well. So that's one example. The other example when you look at combat is that we're giving them the FITS system. So they have four choices there as well. So again, it's not just about the story, it's not just about the combat system, it's about the overall game experience. We're offering them a wide array or a diverse range of options that the players will be able to choose from. And this is something that was also offered in the original FFVII as well. So one of the goals definitely was to recreate that experience through FFVII Revelation.
And we kind of showed a glimpse of this in the State of Play stream, but in certain side quests players will have the choice of which character they would play as. So in the State of Play stream, it showed that players can either choose to play as Vincent or choose to play as Cid. In scenarios like that, depending on the character you go with, the conclusion of the side quest or the way the story plays out could change drastically. So again, that's also another example of the player choices that we're offering for the game experience. All in all, players will be faced with these chances, opportunities where they get to make these choices so that each and every player might have a very unique experience depending on the choices that they made throughout the game.
IGN: So, resolve is a focus of the game. I can't help but notice that word starts with R-E. Was Resolve seriously considered as a subtitle for this game, or were there any other words that start with RE that you were considering?
Hamaguchi: [Laughs] So to answer the first question, “Resolve” was actually not considered as one of the contenders for the title, and there actually is a reason for that. The development team that we have for this game is in Japan and consists of Japanese staff. So when we were having internal discussions about what the core concept or the philosophy of this game was going to be, we did use the term “resolve”, but in Japanese. So in Japanese, the word is called “ketsui”, which as you can tell, doesn't have that RE sound. And then when we were making plans for our first major reveal at Summer Game Fest earlier this year, I actually wrote a script for myself on stage, and I did want to use the term for ketsui, resolve. So when I was looking at the English equivalent of that, I found out that resolve actually started with RE, so I thought, “oh, this is actually a perfect fit!”
I can talk more about how we ended up with the title Revelation. So way before this whole resolve discussion that we had, we did decide to go with the title Revelation, but even before we made that decision, there were actually three final contenders and I had a discussion with the creative director of the series, Tetsuya Nomura.
In terms of the other two contenders that we had aside from Revelation, I might share it sometime in the future, but I don't think now is the right time for us to share it because the game isn’t out yet. If we do share the other two contenders, I don't want people to be like, "Oh, the other one was better than Revelation." And it feels like it's just going to create some unnecessary discussion and debates online. So I feel like now's not the right time. Maybe sometime down the line we might be able to revisit this discussion again and share what the title could have been. But I will say that when I discussed with the North American Square Enix team, I did share the other two options that we had as the final contenders, and we unanimously agreed that Revelation was the best choice. So I think we made the right decision on that.
IGN: Okay, I'll ask you again in a couple of years what the other two were.
IGN: I'd like to talk a little bit more about the combat because Vincent quickly became my go-to character during the preview. And I know you've talked about Vincent a little bit before, but what's maybe your favorite detail that’s gone unnoticed about Vincent's combat style so far?
Endo: I don't think this is something that I can say as something that was unnoticed because I actually addressed this myself during the PAX West stage panel that we had yesterday. But one of my personal favorite functions of Vincent's combat design is that I was able to implement this feature of him being able to turn into the Galian Beast anytime during combat. Just to hold R1 and be able to revert back to human form and go back to the Galian Beast form anytime during combat. Having that in the game, I think that's actually my personal favorite. I'm really glad I was able to do that.
And one of the big reasons why I wanted to implement that was because when you look at the existing party of playable characters, we already have a lot of different options, a lot of different characters that each has its own unique combat experience. So people who have already played Remake and Rebirth might already have their own favorite character to play in combat. So in order for us to deliver a very impactful gameplay experience for these new characters, we needed to make sure that there's something very unique and different about them. So considering that, if we were to follow suit with the original and have this function where Vincent is only able to turn into the Galian Beast only under a specific condition, I don't think that would've been the best way to go about it with the FFVII Remake series. So I think I made the right choice to do that.
So when you think about it, Vincent being able to switch back and forth between his human form and the Galian Beast form, it's essentially two characters packed into one because each form has its own unique movesets and motions as well. So the animation artist had a bit of an extra hard time compared to the other characters trying to implement all these motions into the combat. So in that sense, I think we spent a lot more effort and time developing Vincent's combat system.
IGN: I do want to ask, Revelation is coming out in the last year that Sony is producing physical PlayStation discs, and it is launching with a physical edition. And Final Fantasy VII has this rich history with PlayStation. Was it important to you to have this game release on a physical disc?
Hamaguchi: Last week with the State of Play announcement, we tied it to the preorder as well. So right after the State of Play, the preorders launched. But before we arrived at that decision, there were a lot of internal discussions and back and forth amongst myself and other internal staff members in terms of how we should treat or handle the physical editions. And this whole disc discussion, it is a rather sensitive issue, and I don't think a lot of the media has asked us about this so far. So I would like to discuss how we approached it.
First and foremost, personally, I'm very happy that we are able to release a physical disc version of FFVII Revelation considering how the entire gaming market, or the landscape, is veering towards the disc-less direction. And after we launched preorders, we did see some fans voicing their concerns and raising questions about the physical discs requiring some internet download. So I would like to address that.
When we had an internal discussion with the development team about how we wanted to approach the physical discs and the physical releases of FFVII Revelation, initially there were conversations about using the same disc size as we did for, say, FFVII Rebirth. But if we were to do that, it would mean that we would have to make a compromise in terms of the fidelity and the quality of the game. So as a development team, we didn't want to do that. We didn't want to make any compromises for the game. So realistically, the only choice that we had was to release this physical disc, but with certain sections of the game being a digital download format through the physical disc. With that being said, I completely understand that not all players might be happy with this decision, but at the same time, I am happy that we were still able to release a physical format of the game. So I am quite satisfied with the end results as well. I would hope that our fans and players would be able to share that as well.
IGN: I think it's impressive that you've released a whole trilogy in the span of roughly eight years. That's rare in the video game industry these days. So I'm wondering if there are any learnings from this major project and its development that you can take with you as you move on to whatever's next.
Hamaguchi: I will say that the top priority for us as a team right now is to put a full focus on completing the development of FFVII Revelation. So in terms of what we would do as the next work or the next game, we haven't really put that much of a thought into it right now. That said, looking at the overall landscape and environment of game development, it does seem like creating and developing these AAA titles, it just takes longer and longer as it goes by. So considering that, having this consistent team that's stuck together throughout the last 10 to 12 years, creating the entire trilogy, and being able to gather all this knowledge and experience that can be applied to future development, I think we were in a very lucky position to be able to do that.
But yeah, we are very much eager to utilize and leverage the experiences that we have made throughout these years of development of the FFVII Remake series. I would say it's undecided in terms of the direction that we're going to after the completion of the Remake series, but we hope the fans and players will look forward to what we work on next. But to reiterate our top priority, our full focus is on FFVII Revelation right now. So until we actually complete it and ensure that it's the intended quality that the game should be, I don't think we will have any actual ideas of what we're going to work on next.
IGN: Thank you both so much for your time, and good luck the rest of the way with Revelation. We're looking forward to it.
Hamaguchi and Endo: Thank you.
Parts of this interview were edited for clarity.
Logan Plant is the host of Nintendo Voice Chat and IGN's Senior Editor, Playlist and DB. The Legend of Zelda is his favorite video game franchise of all time, and he is patiently awaiting the day Nintendo announces a brand new F-Zero. You can find new episodes of NVC every Friday on the IGN Games YouTube channel, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or your favorite podcast app.

item.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi has offered an explanation for why the physical disc version of the game on PlayStation 5 and Xbox requires a download to play.
item.description:
Final Fantasy VII Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi has offered an explanation for why the physical disc version of the game on PlayStation 5 and Xbox requires a download to play.
Earlier this month it emerged that the physical version of Final Fantasy VII Revelation on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X comes on a single disc and requires an internet connection to download other parts of the game. The first two games in the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy, Remake and Rebirth, come on two discs: one for installation and one for play. Switch 2 owners get Final Fantasy VII Revelation on a game-key card.
This sparked a backlash among some fans who had hoped for Final Fantasy VII Revelation to be playable without an update, like its predecessors in the long-running franchise. “The game not getting a proper physical release on any platform is the only detail that should be discussed,” commented X / Twitter account Does it play?, which advocates for physical media and has campaigned for video game preservation. “What were you thinking, in all honesty?”
In a new interview with IGN, Hamaguchi suggested that even if Square Enix released Revelation on the same number of discs as Rebirth, it would still have had to “compromise” on the quality of the game. So, the "only choice" it had was to release the game on a single disc with a forced download to play.
“First and foremost, personally, I'm very happy that we are able to release a physical disc version of FFVII Revelation considering how the entire gaming market, or the landscape, is veering towards the disc-less direction,” Hamaguchi said, referencing Sony’s controversial decision to end production of PlayStation discs from 2028.
“And after we launched preorders, we did see some fans voicing their concerns and raising questions about the physical discs requiring some internet download. So I would like to address that.
“When we had an internal discussion with the development team about how we wanted to approach the physical discs and the physical releases of FFVII Revelation, initially there were conversations about using the same disc size as we did for, say, FFVII Rebirth. But if we were to do that, it would mean that we would have to make a compromise in terms of the fidelity and the quality of the game. So as a development team, we didn't want to do that. We didn't want to make any compromises for the game. So realistically, the only choice that we had was to release this physical disc, but with certain sections of the game being a digital download format through the physical disc.”
Hamaguchi went on to acknowledge fan complaints around this, but insisted he’s happy with where Square Enix ended up on the issue.
“With that being said, I completely understand that not all players might be happy with this decision, but at the same time, I am happy that we were still able to release a physical format of the game,” he said. “So I am quite satisfied with the end results as well. I would hope that our fans and players would be able to share that as well.”
Final Fantasy VII Revelation is due out across PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, and Nintendo Switch 2, on April 8, 2027.

item.title: Project Zeta is a mashup of multiple live-service genres, but for developer Nirvanana, it’s best described as an “espresso MOBA.”
item.description:
Project Zeta is a mashup of multiple live-service genres, but for developer Nirvanana, it’s best described as an “espresso MOBA.”
This four-teams-of-three ‘Tactical Hero Arena’ third-person action game is, essentially, a race involving as many teamfights as possible. The game actively encourages teams to fight each other, scrapping over objectives throughout each phase of a session. MOBAs typically focus combat down lanes, but in Project Zeta, around three minutes into each session, the focus becomes fighting over objectives. You have to seek out teamfights to win. This is not a game about hiding in bushes.
Each session is made up of seven phases. The first phase sees players defeat ordinary monsters to level up — all very MOBA. It’s a warmup phase meant to give players breathing room to develop a strategy. Generally, you’re on the hunt for prisms, which drop from prism bosses. Grab one then take it to one of the ballasts in the center of the map to score a point. The first team to score five points wins, exiting the game in first place.
“What we're aiming to deliver is a removal of the lane-ing in traditional MOBAs,” Nirvanana CEO Namseok Kim told me at gamescom 2026. “It's objective-driven with a lot of teamfights. So that compressed experience is what we're looking for. As fans of the MOBA genre, we believe that the fun of MOBAs comes from playing smart and winning the teamfights. And we need it so that you can enjoy an endless supply of that kind of experience in the compressed 20-minute time of a session. It's going to be a very dense experience. So we wanted to propose a new kind of MOBA.”
Another unique aspect of Project Zeta is its lack of a crosshair at the center of the screen, which you typically see in hero shooters and 3D MOBAs. This means basic attacks always land. More accurate aim does not factor into fights; instead, the idea is that success comes from your understanding of the each hero's abilities, mind games, and positioning. Combat is a sort of dance between dodging enemy attacks and making sure your attacks land.
Reducing downtime, players in eliminated teams are immediately revived with their cooldowns and HP restored. Battle royale MOBAs typically restrict players to a limited number of lives, so players play passively in order to survive. Project Zeta has a score race with unlimited respawns and a quick time-to-kill. The game wants players to take risks to eliminate other teams, and because everything is restored once a team is eliminated, the hope is that players won’t shy away from getting into scraps.
“We wanted the sessions to feel like a Formula 1 race,” Namseok Kim said. “Everyone is racing toward these objectives. That is what Project Zeta is.”
Like a racing game, Project Zeta displays a scoreboard on the top left that fluctuates as teams turn prisms in. “Everything needs to happen in 20 minutes,” Namseok Kim explained. “So everything that makes a MOBA fun is compressed into that short time. Yesterday, one journalist said that if other MOBAs are coffee, then Project Zeta could be like instant espresso. And we agreed, that was a great analogy. We had made up the term ‘multi-team tactical arena’ to describe Project Zeta, but personally I like ‘espresso MOBA’ better.”
Namseok Kim said that one of the reasons he made Project Zeta is because his daughter thought a game of Riot Games’ League of Legends took too long. “There's too much to learn,” he said. “There's too much to memorize. And I played League of Legends with her 10 times and every time she didn't like it. I made Project Zeta to help her approach MOBAs, and I think that would maybe make the concept accessible.”
It’s also worth noting that Project Zeta was built from the ground up to be playable on a controller, with the goal that PC and console players can compete on a level playing field. There’s also an auto-itemization scheme. Outside of a session, you can set up your skills in advance to focus more on aggression, support, or defense, and then when you enter a session, Project Zeta will automatically purchase the necessary skills for you.
Reinforcing the focus on quickfire combat, Project Zeta has no pure tankers or pure healers. “Personally, I think pure tankers and pure healers are kind of boring!” Namseok Kim said. “And if we had these kinds of characters, it drastically increases the time-to-kill. And if you have a longer time-to-kill, in a session, the third team that joins is usually the most advantageous because A and B are already engaged in combat. And even if A… they won, if their HP is already low, they're tired. And if the third team comes in, they're probably going to have the upper hand. In order to guarantee the proactiveness of a multi-team, we have to have a short time-to-kill. And that's why we don't have pure tankers or pure healers.”
The question for Nirvanana, of course, is will Project Zeta have enough of a pull to drag MOBA fans away from their current favorite game. Will players ditch League of Legends or Dota 2, for example, to give it a try, at a time when most video game companies are finding it increasingly difficult to make a dent in the established players? The fast-paced nature of the game, its streamlined design, and its availability on console may help it stand out.
Project Zeta, developed by Nirvanana Studio and published by PUBG company Krafton, is currently confirmed for PC via Steam and PlayStation 5.

item.title: GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games has issued a new statement as it heads to an employment tribunal to face allegations that it unlawfully fired 31 workers.
item.description:
GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games will today appear before an employment tribunal to face allegations from a union that it unlawfully fired 31 workers in October last year.
The hearing, which kicks off at Glasgow Employment Tribunal this morning, will air allegations made by the Independent Workers of Great Britain union (IWGB) — allegations Rockstar Games strongly denies. The IWGB will claim that the staff, who were all working on GTA 6, were unlawfully blacklisted and targeted for their union activities, and that the manner in which they were dismissed was also unlawful because, the union claims, it came without disciplinary process or right of appeal.
Rockstar has insisted the employees it fired were dismissed because they leaked GTA 6 game features in Discord, not because they were trying to unionize. 34 members of staff at Rockstar were dismissed — 31 in the UK and three in Canada — sparking protests outside the office of Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland, and parent company Take-Two in London.
In a new statement issued to IGN, a spokesperson for Rockstar Games insisted the studio was ready to defend itself from the claims. The statement is below:
“Rockstar Games' position has been clear and consistent throughout. Individuals across the UK and Canada were dismissed for gross misconduct following the sharing of confidential company information, not because of alleged trade union membership or activity. We reject the claims and will defend them vigorously before the tribunal.”
The hearing will run until October 16, a month before GTA 6 comes out. The workers want reinstatement or, failing that, compensation, as well as a finding from the tribunal that their dismissals were unfair. The IWGB alleges that on the day of the dismissals, employees were called into meetings, told they were being fired with immediate effect and escorted from the building. Workers who were not at the office allege they were informed during phone calls lasting around two minutes before being locked out of their work accounts. The IWGB also alleges that one of the dismissed workers, Will Mesilane, had to leave the UK and return to Australia after Rockstar withdrew his work visa and reported him to the Home Office, without giving him a chance to appeal.
Jason Lewis, former Rockstar employee and IWGB Union member, commented: “For almost a year, the truth about what happened to us has been buried by Rockstar and surrounded by speculation. Now we finally get the chance to put it on the record. None of us imagined that talking to each other about our working conditions would turn our lives upside down and catapult us into the centre of a global media storm. As the world prepares for the release of GTA 6, we are reliving the heartbreak of being thrown out of a project we poured so much of our lives into. We lost our jobs, our income, our community and the chance to see the game through to release after spending years helping to build it. It was devastating.
“We have fought tooth and nail to get to this point, not just to be able to win justice for ourselves, but to draw a line in the sand for any employer that thinks it can attack workers for unionising. It has been an emotional journey and it is not over yet, but we can now see the finish line, and justice at last feels within reach.”
Rockstar Games insists there is no link to union activity, and that at the time of the dismissals it didn’t know that the people it fired were involved with a union. As for the Discord comments at the heart of this case, Rockstar says they had to do with GTA 6 features, overall progress and timelines to launch, as well as company IT security protocols. Rockstar believes that if the Discord comments had leaked they would have been big gaming news and might even have affected Take-Two’s share price. When Rockstar officially announced that GTA 6 would be delayed by six months to November 19, 2026, the market value of Take-Two plummeted $3.75 billion in a single day.
Rockstar has also pointed to its well-established zero tolerance approach to leaks, highlighting that it dismissed a Rockstar employee in Lincoln, UK in April 2025, who it alleged disclosed confidential information about GTA 6 to a third party who published the information to social media, and dismissed an employee in the U.S. in November 2023 and another in India in November 2025 for two separate acts of information leaking.
Rockstar’s rules around confidentiality are known to be much stronger than those at many other companies, and it insists every employee understands this. As is well documented, Rockstar is a very secretive company — indeed, Rhys Elliot, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, recently told IGN that the celebrated developer has a “near-pathological” approach to confidentiality. It maintains that the Discord channel where the comments in question were posted was not private for employees only, but contained hundreds of people, including, Rockstar alleges, employees of rival game developers, a game industry journalist, and other unidentifiable members. The IWGB denies this, insisting the Discord channel was private.
Last month, the fired Rockstar workers told fans they shouldn’t boycott GTA 6 to protest on their behalf, but buy T-shirts launched to raise money towards their legal costs instead. Meanwhile, negotiations are ongoing between Rockstar and the IWGB over formal union recognition, even amid this legal battle. The union wants greater pay transparency, protection from post-release layoffs, an end to "crunch," and improved flexible working arrangements, it’s said. If an agreement is reached, Rockstar would become the biggest recognised unionised game studio in the UK. Workers hope to secure recognition before the release of GTA 6.
Alex Marshall, president of the IWGB, said: “We believe Rockstar has tried to get away with Grand Theft Employment Rights. After a year of fighting to get answers, we hope this tribunal will finally back them into a corner and bring the truth to light. As the world gets its first proper look at GTA 6, this hearing will give people a chance to look behind the scenes at what happened to the workers who helped make it.
“That is why this hearing matters for every worker across the UK, whether their job is in entertainment, education or anywhere else. It is a moment to send a clear message to each of them: you have the right to join a union, that right is protected by law, and employers cannot punish you for exercising it.
“If Rockstar can get away with firing workers for organising, then every employer in Britain gets the message that they can do the same. We cannot let that happen.”
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Nintendo has released a fresh firmware update, adding VRR support to Switch 2.
item.description:
Nintendo has released a fresh firmware update for its Switch and Switch 2 consoles, adding VRR support while playing Switch 2 in TV mode.
The ability to toggle on VRR, or variable refresh rate, will of course also rely on your TV supporting this feature. Still, if it does, you'll be able to toggle this on — though bear in mind you'll also just need to activate an update to your Switch 2's dock first. (Finally, Welcome Tour's VRR minigame will be fully playable!)
You'll also now be able to perform a system transfer between two Switch 2 consoles, which will be handy if you're picking up that upcoming Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 special edition console and want to move all your games and settings over.
A list of other smaller tweaks lies below for both consoles, though the majority of additions here are for Nintendo's newer machine:
We took the following actions in the “GameChat”:
You can check the registration status of the device using the virtual game card.
VRR output is now supported in TV mode. When both the software and the TV support it, the video will be output at a refresh rate that matches the game’s processing speed. An update to the Nintendo Switch 2 Dock is required to enable this feature.
Nintendo Switch 2 now supports “complete data transfer” between two Nintendo Switch 2 consoles. You can transfer all your data, including save data and screenshots, from your Switch 2 to your new Switch 2 console.
Made the following changes in “Settings”.
Even if you cannot transfer the virtual game card from another console when starting the software, you can now temporarily play the software using an online license. If another console is offline and you are unable to transfer the virtual game card, the “Play with Online License” button will appear. Only the person who purchased the software can play it using an online license.

item.title: Unlike PlayStation and Xbox, which offer multiple ways to verify you’re over 18, Valve will only accept ownership of an actual credit card, despite the fact only about half of Australian consumers actually have one.
item.description:
Valve has implemented a proof-of-age verification system for Australian Steam users, which was required due to new laws in the country forcing online gaming platforms to require users to prove they are over 18 years of age to access games classified R18+. That law actually came into effect way back in March.
However, unlike PlayStation and Xbox (which offer multiple ways to verify you’re over 18), Valve has opted that it will only accept ownership of an actual credit card as sufficient proof of age. Despite some users anecdotally reporting otherwise, it does not appear debit cards are sufficient, and nor is PayPal. It also doesn’t matter if your Steam account is already well over 20 years old.
Without verification, Australian Steam users trying to access the store page of a game rated R18+ will be met by the following message:
“Valve is required by the Age-Restricted Material App Distribution Services Code to verify that you are 18 or older before accessing mature content. If you wish to do so, please add a valid Australian credit card to your account and afterwards update the Mature Content Preferences.”
Of course, not all Australian Steam users over 18 have a credit card, or indeed want a credit card – when there are already a ton of more convenient ways to make purchases online. Unfortunately for Australian Steam users, an active credit card is all Valve is willing to accept, despite other methods of verification being readily available. This active credit card also reportedly needs to remain active on the account, even if you do not want to make purchases with it.
The fact that Valve’s proof-of-age verification “system” has come so late and yet is so unfit for purpose is either arrogance or naivety on the company’s part, considering how significantly credit card ownership in Australia has fallen over the past decade. Today, only around half of Australian consumers even have a credit card, with adoption lowest amongst young adults (only around a quarter of Australian consumers aged 18 to 24 have a credit card). Credit cards are entirely unnecessary to make online purchases in 2026, and Valve should have known better considering its payment option data in Australia ought to have made that more than evident.
IGN has contacted Valve for comment.
Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

item.title: Renowned video game director Hideo Kojima's upcoming project Physint, which could fairly be described as a spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, will now be published by Xbox instead of Sony, Microsoft announced today. item.description:
Renowned video game director Hideo Kojima's upcoming project Physint, which could fairly be described as a spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, will now be published by Xbox instead of Sony, Microsoft announced today.
Xbox will continue to publish Kojima's horror game OD — itself something of a spiritual successor to the never-finished PT — and the Kojima-Xbox partnership will expand beyond these two game projects to include film and television.
“This expands our relationship with Xbox beyond OD. As we move forward with the development of Physint, we remain committed to redefining the action-espionage genre for players around the world,” Kojima said.
He also posted on X with details on how the deal came to be, saying that Sony was going to cancel Physint. "As confirmed earlier through our official channels, in mid-June of this year, we unexpectedly received notice from PlayStation Studios that they would cancel the Physint project. Physint is an important project both to me personally and to Kojima Productions. Determined to keep the project alive, we have spent the last three months searching tirelessly for a new partner. In the course of seeking advice and pursuing negotiations with people across many fields, we found in Xbox a partner with whom we share a common vision for the future, and we have decided to team up with them once again. Please rest assured that development of Physint, our genre-defining action-espionage title, is ongoing and will continue moving forward."
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who took over from the retiring Phil Spencer earlier this year, made Kojima a priority in her quest to reset and rebuild Xbox, including the return of console exclusives that begins with Gears of War: E-Day this year and continues with Clockwork Revolution in 2027. In terms of Kojima Productions projects, OD will be released before Physint. In July, IGN reported that OD was safe from Sharma's big "reset" of the Xbox business, which has seen thousands of staff lose their jobs, multiple studios go independent, and various video game projects canceled.
“Creators have choices about where and how they bring their ideas to life," Sharma said. "We’re honored that Kojima-san has chosen Xbox to work with Kojima Productions on Physint. His ambition to challenge conventions reflects the kind of creativity we want to support at Xbox.”
PlayStation issued a statement as well, posting, "After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to step away from collaborating with Kojima Productions on its project Physint. We continue to have great admiration for Hideo Kojima's vision for the game. Our relationship remains strong after three decades of industry-leading, genre-defining creative cooperation, and we look forward to continued close collaboration with Hideo Kojima and his award-winning independent studio in the future."
When Physint was announced it was heavily backed by Sony. During the 2024 State of Play broadcast, PlayStation Studios boss Hermen Hulst shook Kojima's hand while saying: "Today, I'm excited to announce that together, as part of the PlayStation and Kojima Productions partnership, Hideo's going to take us on an exciting new adventure, one that I've been encouraging him to reinvent for years." Hulst continued: "We're are all really excited about this project, and we weill fully support you with the latest innovations Sony has to offer. More details to come."
Kojima and Hulst ended the announcement by walking off set, the camera pulling away out of the building to reveal a Columbia Pictures sign with the word 'Physint' below it. (Columbia Pictures is owned by the Sony Group Corporation through its subsidiary, Sony Pictures Entertainment.)
The switch from PlayStation to Xbox is a major PR win for Microsoft, which has effectively stolen a Kojima project away from Sony. The last time one first-party platform lost out to another on this kind of AAA level — and the only one I can think of — is when Final Fantasy jumped ship from Nintendo to PlayStation back in the PS1 era.
Physint is a working title, and we still don't know much about it. "Of course, it is an interactive game," Kojima said when Physint was announced, "but it is also a movie at the same time." He continued: "It is a completely new 'Action Espionage' for the next-generation. It will be created using cutting-edge technology and the best talents from around the world, both from film and video games. Of course this is an interactive 'game,' but the look, story, theme, cast, acting, fashion, sound, etc... are all at the next level of 'Digital Entertainment' that could be called a 'movie.'"
It may be some time before Physint comes out, as Kojima said last year that Physint was likely another 5-6 years away. But work on the game is ramping up. Just this week, many fans were left convinced that Batman actor Robert Pattinson will star in the game.
Kojima last officially discussed Physint in September 2025, during a Kojima Productions 10th Anniversary event in Japan. Speaking on-stage during the event, Kojima said development on Physint was just starting, and that he was working on concepts by himself, making characters, and thinking about casting. The tech underpinning Physint was described as even more advanced than that powering Kojima’s Death Stranding games and OD (whose debut trailer was revealed at the show).
Kojima did tease the main character of the game via the first poster for Physint, below.
Kojima also confirmed three actors set to appear in Physint, each of whom delivered a video message expressing their excitement. Charlee Fraser, who played Mary Jabassa in Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga, is in the game, although we don’t know which character she’s playing. Also in the game are Don Lee, who played Gilgamesh in the Marvel movie Eternals, and Japanese actress Minami Hamabe, who played Noriko Ōishi in Godzilla Minus One.
Kojima ended his Physint segment with a shot of Hamabe in CG form, showing off just how realistic the visuals are expected to be. We still don't know which game engine Kojima Productions is using for Physint.
Photo by TheStewartofNY/GC Images.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: A hacker using an ‘Evil’ Tung Tung Tung Sahur skin has been banned after wreaking havoc in Valorant lobbies and decimating entire teams.
item.description:
A hacker using an ‘Evil’ Tung Tung Tung Sahur skin has been banned after wreaking havoc in Valorant lobbies and decimating entire teams.
Cheaters are a never-ending issue in online multiplayer games, but some are more memorable than others. A recent hacking incident has produced possibly one of the most memorable cheaters of all — or at least, one of the most visually disturbing.
As pointed out by Dexerto, a hacker using an ‘Evil’ Tung Tung Tung Sahur skin has sparked backlash within the Valorant community, and it’s not hard to see why. The skin, modeled after the viral brainrot meme Tung Tung Tung Sahur, has transformed the character into a deranged-looking, evil version of himself. (I choose to believe that Evil Tung Tung Tung Sahur is the ‘Evil Ryu’ to Tung Tung Tung Sahur’s normal form.)
Evil Tung activities | #VALORANT pic.twitter.com/wQaPMF7TxD
Footage of the hacker went viral on social media, showing the cheater in third-person from what appears to be their own perspective. We can see the outlines of enemies through walls as Evil Tung walks backwards, shooting his gun at nothing — only for his opponents to drop like flies in a blink.
This video showed that the cheater seemed to have enabled wallhacks and auto-targeting, but it’s uncertain if they were using any other methods to decimate these lobbies. It took the Valorant community by storm, prompting popular analyst ‘vladk0r’ to post it as a jab against Riot's kernel-level anti-cheat system, Vanguard.
“Imagine losing to a team with this s**t only for them being banned later after [a] few rounds of the bracket, and not being able to do anything with this, ‘cause they got DQ’d much later after your match, so Riot can't revert the results,” he wrote.
“Proof that kernel-level anti-cheat compromises user privacy and security for nothing,” another player argued. “Cheaters own and control the hardware the game runs on, they always find a way eventually. You don't need more privilege in a client-side AC, you need server-side AC and behavioural analysis.”
“Kernel-level anti-cheat really thought it could stop Tung Tung Tung Cheat-Hur,” another joked.
Thankfully, Valorant lobbies weren’t plagued for much longer; Riot’s anti-cheat director Phillip Koskinas responded to the issue in a tweet confirming that the cheater had been banned, along with their Riot ID, the name of their cheat (which Koskinas dubbed ‘lowskill vibeslop’), and how many games they’d played.
“We can detect anything with time, but VAL is a free to play game. Agree that we have to improve pre-emptive posture for open qualifiers,” he wrote, adding that it was “pointless” to hide the hacker’s Riot ID.
Riot ID: FaeL o Anacondo#br1Banned: 2026-09-03Games Played: 3Cheat Name: "Sysinfo" (lowskill vibeslop)Hiding the Riot ID: PointlessWe can detect anything with time, but VAL is a free to play game. Agree that we have to improve pre-emptive posture for open qualifiers. https://t.co/4h1GpajkuQ
This dastardly, if disturbingly creative, cheater finally got what was coming to them after ruining games for so many players. Evil Tung Tung Tung Sahur’s wrath has ended.

item.title: Today's September 2026 Nintendo Direct has come and gone, and so has any chance of seeing the next 3D Mario, The Duskbloods, and more highly anticipated games that ended up being no-shows.
item.description:
Today's September 2026 Nintendo Direct has come and gone, and so has any chance of seeing the next 3D Mario, The Duskbloods, and more highly anticipated games that ended up being no-shows.
Nintendo covered a lot in this morning's 45-minute slot. Metroid Ravenous is bringing Samus back for another 2D adventure, Kirby and the World Beyond is going 3D in 2027, and Mario Kart World is finally getting some much-needed love with a new update. Nintendo Switch 2 owners are eating well in more ways than one, but many fans say they were left starving for something a little more filling.
For instance, the company's hybrid sequel console is barreling through its second year without a proper 3D Mario to call its own. The Duskbloods, FromSoftware's vampire-themed Switch 2 exclusive multiplayer game, was nowhere to be seen despite still carrying a 2026 release window. Rumors suggesting new Super Smash Bros., Nintendogs, and Luigi's Mansion games were in the works really only helped build the mountain of no-shows overshadowing the show in fans' minds.
Despite yesterday's Zelda anniversary stream packing in some big announcements, Nintendo players largely seem to agree that, save for the Metroid and Kirby highlights, today's September Direct could have packed a bigger punch as the year winds down. It's a lot to go over, but we've gathered all of the biggest absent games from the September 2026 Direct, regardless of whether they've actually been announced or not.
Even after a year of updates, the Elden Ring and Dark Souls developer has never wavered when it comes to the release schedule for its new game. As details have snowballed into the public consciousness in recent months, it feels like the only thing fans don't know about the game is its actual release date.
Today's Direct seemed like a perfect opportunity to pin something down on the calendar, so when it came to a close with Kirby and not Zork, fans grew concerned. It doesn't help that a recent network test didn't exactly go off without a hitch.
So, has The Duskbloods been delayed? Well, no – or at least not yet – but if FromSoftware still wants to see it out before the year is up, it's running out of time to make a proper announcement.
WHERE IS DUSKBLOODS pic.twitter.com/isvoF0FsKb
What is Next Level Games up to? The Mario Strikers and Luigi's Mansion series developer was officially acquired by Nintendo in 2021, but aside from assisting with the development of 2025's Metroid Prime 4, the studio's last headlining release was 2022's Mario Strikers: Battle League.
Couple that with the fact that it's been almost seven years since the team put out Luigi's Mansion 3, and you've got a recipe for fans on social media to wonder what's going on. Nintendo hasn't officially announced a new entry in Mario's brother's ghost-hunting series, but considering the last mainline game's success, many are hoping we'll hear from Next Level with a Luigi's Mansion 4 sooner rather than later.
https://t.co/FncmMJVNdA pic.twitter.com/KwOhwlcBzT
Again, a new Animal Crossing game isn't something Nintendo has explicitly announced, but that hasn't stopped fans from clamoring for more. The last time Tom Nook came to take players' Bells in a more formal manner was with 2020's monumental original Switch game Animal Crossing: New Horizons.
A Switch 2 version also gave villagers new reasons to return to their island getaways in January of this year, and Nintendo historically favoring long breaks between mainline releases. Despite all of this, fans weren't happy to see that a new Animal Crossing game didn't make an appearance.
Me because they didn’t announce animal crossing pic.twitter.com/A9pX0y7DLc
So... no animal crossing mention in the nintendo direct??pic.twitter.com/gWtneLgaOk
I know what you're thinking: 'But Mario Kart World did show up in the Nintendo Direct' – and you're right. Today's shadow drop is one of the open-world kart racer's biggest yet, bringing reimagined SNES courses for players to race through, free of charge. It's a nice addition, but judging by reactions across social media and even in our very own comment sections, Nintendo could have done more.
"Anything to avoid giving us new costumes or original tracks, huh?" one IGN reader commented on our update reveal story. "Better than nothing, I suppose, but still – I'm curious what Nintendo's long-term plans for this game are."
There's nothing really stopping the company from holding off on outfits or character DLC for a while longer. After all, Mario Kart 8 went on to receive add-on content in the form of its Deluxe release's Booster Course Pass years after its original launch. When or if more is on the way is unclear, but it's probably best if fans don't write off Mario Kart World just yet.
omfg just give us new characters and actual new tracks already pic.twitter.com/JLQpDCv9XN
While something like The Duskbloods felt like a shoo-in, a new mainline 3D Mario game was never quite as certain. That didn't make its absence sting any less, though.
Super Mario Odyssey's launch trailed behind the original Switch's release by about eight months. Now, 15 months removed from the launch of the Switch 2, we're still without a new 3D romp for everyone's favorite Goomba-stomping plumber.
"10 years without a 3D Mario game is f**king pathetic I'm sorry," one popular X/Twitter post said. "But hey, at least we get our second 3D Kirby in five years!!!!!"
Yes, yes, the wonderful Donkey Kong Bananza has helped fill the nine-year void, but that's not changing the temperature for fans online who were hoping Nintendo's Yoshiaki Koizumi would have had more to share during the show.
this direct really felt like this pic.twitter.com/ctVOxfhqZA
Here's where fan expectations veered from hopes to dreams thanks to recent rumors and leaks that started when notable leaker Malo932 spilled a few beans earlier this week. item.title: Three fan-favorite Batman movies are being re-released in theaters next week in celebration of Batman Day.
item.description:
Three fan-favorite Batman movies are being re-released in theaters next week in celebration of Batman Day.
Warner Bros. has announced some big plans for Batman Day next week, one of which includes a whole weekend of Batman films in theaters. The studio will be re-releasing Tim Burton's Batman, Batman: Mask of the Phantasm, and The LEGO Batman Movie at participating AMC, Cinemark, and Regal theaters. However, feel free to check other chains as well; I also found a few smaller theaters playing some of these films.
The rollout will begin on Friday, September 18, with one movie playing each night throughout the weekend. According to listings, Batman will play on September 18, Mask of the Phantasm will screen on September 19, and The LEGO Batman Movie will be shown on September 20. In the past, theaters have shown Christopher Nolan's Dark Knight trilogy during this period, but that doesn't appear to be the case this year. Instead, TNT will be airing the trilogy on TV on September 19, and of course, they'll also be available to stream on HBO Max.
While most fans have likely seen Burton's Batman at some point in their lives, it's worth seeing big and loud in a movie theater, if given the opportunity. Batman: Mask of the Phantasm is also well worth seeing in theaters, as it had a theatrical release back in the 90s, but not many people actually made it to the theater to check it out. It's arguably one of the best Batman films out there, and if you haven't seen it at all, there's no better way to experience it than on the big screen.
In related news, Batman's next big-screen adventure is still a ways off. The Batman Part 2 starring Robert Pattinson is officially filming throughout the rest of the year and will hit theaters in February 2027, after years of production delays. The film's plot and villains are being kept under wraps, but Sebastian Stan is heavily rumored and speculated to play Harvey Dent/Two Face.

item.title: The 23rd and final novel in Brian Jacques’ Redwall series will be published in September 2027, putting an end to the beloved saga after 41 years.
item.description:
The 23rd and final novel in Brian Jacques’ Redwall series will be published in September 2027, putting an end to the beloved saga after 41 years.
The late, great Jacques still has one more ace up his sleeve. Orphans of Mossflower, the very last Redwall book penned by the celebrated British author, will be released posthumously alongside the saga’s first-ever box set next year.
As spotted by a post on the official Redwall fan Wiki, the digital publishing catalog platform Edelweiss features a frontlist of forthcoming Redwall books, which includes Orphans of Mossflower. As told by the frontlist, this will be the “final book in the series.”
Nothing else about the title was shared, but it’s expected to be a direct sequel to the series’ most recent book, The Rogue Crew — which was published in 2011, a whopping 15 years ago.
Jacques died that same year at 71 after suffering a heart attack. The Rogue Crew was the only Redwall book to be published after his death, meaning that Orphans of Mossflower will be the second. It’s unclear if any additions were made to the novel by his editors, or how far along it was at the time of his death — but we suspect we’ll learn the answers to these questions when it gets closer to being released next year.
For now, theories abound as to what adventures Mossflower's creatures will get up to in this last novel. One hypothesis points to the winner of a 2010 contest who got to create a character that would appear in a future Redwall novel. This character was initially suspected to be in The Rogue Crew, but that didn’t happen — and given that Jacques died shortly before it was published, fans are of the mind that this character might pop up in Orphans of Mossflower.
Speaking to those at the Redwall Wiki, the winner — named Olivia — said she created a haremaiden named Reisa Kartwell, explaining that "’Reisa’ comes from ‘reise,’ meaning ‘travel’ in German, and ‘Kartwell’ is derived from ‘karte,’ the German word for ‘map.’ Reisa is Salamandastron's cartographer, and her map depicting efficient travel paths proves invaluable when the Redwallers must quickly reach Salamandastron when Redwall is under attack.”
The Rogue Crew follows Abbot Thibb, the Longpatrol hares, and the titular rogue crew of sea otters as they defend Redwall Abbey from the vicious Razzid Wearat, who wreaks havoc on his wheeled ship that can traverse both land and sea. We’ll have to see where this story picks up in the final book when it’s published a year from now.
This news follows the sad cancellation of Netflix’s Redwall series earlier this year. Fans of animal-fantasy literature need not worry, though; Erin Hunter’s Warriors book saga is getting a long-awaited animated series on Disney+, as well as a video game, the latter of which will release in October 2026.

item.title: Writer-director Michael Mann is taking another crack at his 2006 film, Miami Vice. Miami Vice: Director’s Final Cut will make its world premiere at Beyond Fest in Los Angeles on October 3, 2026.
item.description:
Writer-director Michael Mann is taking another crack at his 2006 film, Miami Vice.
It was announced today that Miami Vice: Director’s Final Cut will make its world premiere at Beyond Fest in Los Angeles on October 3, 2026, followed by a Q&A with Mann.
It is described as “Michael Mann’s new cut” and that it will be shown in 4K. The Beyond Fest site doesn’t list the running time of this new cut.
If this version is truly a “new cut" then it will be an even different version of the film than the Miami Vice: Unrated Director’s Edition that was released on Blu-ray in 2008. The Unrated Director’s Edition is a re-edited film featuring scenes that were cut from the theatrical release as well as new music cues.
“These changes are enough to make this Miami Vice a slightly different and in some ways better experience than the theatrical cut, although the film's same fundamental flaws remain,” as I wrote in my review of the Unrated Director’s Edition at the time.
“This edition, however, is closer in tone to the TV series [which Mann exec produced but did not create], enough to have muted some of that criticism. For example, it opens with an offshore speedboat race set against the sunny Miami skyline and scored with electronic music, which conjures memories of the series' opening credits.”
Mann’s Miami Vice was a legendarily difficult production, culminating in the abrupt departure of lead actor Jamie Foxx, who played Detective Ricardo Tubbs opposite Colin Farrell as his partner, Sonny Crockett. Foxx abandoned the film during shooting in the Dominican Republic, a move that forced Mann to change the movie’s ending.
Although Miami Vice opened in first place at the domestic box office in 2006, it ultimately proved a commercial and critical misfire. However, the film has earned a cult status and critical reappraisal in the two decades since its release.
F1’s Joseph Kosinski will direct a big screen reboot, Miami Vice ‘85, that will star Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler. That film will be released on May 19, 2028.

item.title: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy has re-emerged, five years after its release, with a new Switch 2 version... and some fans hope it could lead to a sequel.
item.description:
Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy has re-emerged, five years after its release, with a new Switch 2 version... and some fans hope it could lead to a sequel.
During today's Nintendo Direct, fans were surprised to learn that Eidos Montreal's Guardians of the Galaxy game is coming back. It's getting a new "Encore Edition," exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2, which not only brings the game to a new platform, but also adds new content like special outfits for the cosmic heroes. This news came as a bit of a shock, since the game missed sales expectations despite having great reviews, so fans assumed that we'd never see this iteration of the Guardians ever again.
Now, this new release has some hoping that the Guardians may live on. Over on social media, excited fans are pleading to Marvel and Eidos Montreal to produce a sequel. Maybe a Switch 2 version could be used to test the waters, but it's hard to say. Either way, it's great to see such a beloved game finding its way back into the market, and hopefully, it can create some demand for another entry in the series.
"Don’t sleep on this game, Switch players. It’s fu**ing dope," said one fan. "Do yourself a favor and pick this up! It’s a GREAT game! I hate the fact that this gem got overlooked (and Midnight Suns as well btw)," noted another.
"Can we just get a sequel? The people have been asking for years," asked another fan. "Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy 2, please," another pleaded.
These are far from the only people asking for a sequel or begging new players to check it out; the comments under the announcement posts from Marvel Games and the game's official account are flooded with similar responses.
Guardians of the Galaxy has seemingly had legs over the years. A year after its release, the team behind the game announced it had reached 8 million players, partially thanks to the game's inclusion on services like Xbox Game Pass. It's unclear how many people have played it since then, but it's frequently deeply discounted, so the numbers have likely only grown a fair bit in the last four years. Eidos Montreal also stated that it had no regrets over the game, despite it not being a big seller.
Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition will hit Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5. Whether it gets overshadowed by the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remains to be seen, but hopefully it can find a new audience on the platform.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword dropped last week, and we’re of the opinion that it’s a 10/10 masterpiece.
If you’ve already jumped into the action or are generally curious about the story side of things, it's worth checking out the official companion webcomic. The story serves as a direct prequel to Way of the Sword, and is free to read for anyone with a Webtoon account.
The entire Onimusha series takes place in an alternate version of Japan’s feudal era. In the game’s canon timeline, Way of the Sword picks up over two decades after the previous mainline release, Dawn of Dreams, bringing the world of Genma into the Edo period.
The companion webcomic, subtitled "Fated Rivalry," picks up pretty soon before the main events of Way of the Sword. The story follows Miyamoto Musashi's rival, Sasaki Ganryu, who discovers an Oni Gauntlet on his vengeance-driven quest to become powerful enough to take down Musashi.
The prequel is being produced by Laurel Pursuit, a US-based studio that’s previously distributed the Dungeon Crawler Carl graphic novel as well as original webcomics like Defiance of the Fall. The Onimusha webcomic specifically features work from Webtoon creators jjolee, hilluhri, and BAEKSSE.
The first chapter was released this past Saturday and has amassed just over 20,000 clicks so far. Future chapters will continue to become available on Saturdays, though it’s unclear how long the full prequel webcomic will end up being.
Here’s the full description of the comic, which is free to read with a Webtoon account:
When you live by the way of the sword, there’s only room for one at the top.
Sasaki Ganryu has one goal: to become the strongest swordsman in the world. When a duel with the wandering samurai Miyamoto Musashi ends in humiliating defeat, Ganryu is consumed by rage. What follows is a bloody quest to reclaim his honor that leads him down a path of madness and obsession.
On his journey, he receives a mysterious artifact known as “The Oni Gauntlet”, that gives him a power no mortal blade could ever match. Hunting down ever-stronger foes has set him on a collision course to face off again against the only man who has ever bested him in battle.
A prologue to the latest game in Capcom’s iconic samurai action series: Onimusha: Way of the Sword.
This isn’t the first time Onimusha has extended beyond the gaming realm. A film based on the action series was pitched all the way back in the early 2000s, but was eventually canceled. What did eventually come to fruition was an anime adaptation, released on Netflix in 2023.
Most fans don’t consider that story canon to the games. The webcomic, in contrast, flows pretty much seamlessly into Way of the Sword while staying faithful to events from previous games in the series.

item.title: The fighting game community is in the middle of a fierce debate over the amount of guest characters coming to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves.
item.description:
The fighting game community is in the middle of a fierce debate over the amount of guest characters coming to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves.
On September 9, SNK announced two more guest characters coming to City of the Wolves: Manjiro "Mikey" Sano and Ken "Draken" Ryuguji from Tokyo Revengers. These popular shonen anime protagonists mark the latest in a string of guest characters for the game, which include Chun-Li and Ken from Street Fighter, pro footballer Cristiano Ronaldo, music artist Salvatore Ganacci, and Kenshiro from Fist of the North Star.
That’s a lot of guest characters for a game that’s only a little more than a year old — and while Ken and Chun-Li make sense given Capcom and SNK’s wealth of crossovers over the years, five guest characters from totally unrelated franchises feels a bit excessive to some players (myself included).
There’s a trend sweeping through popular fighting games lately where non-fighting game characters are being included in major titles like Street Fighter 6, Tekken 8, and of course, City of the Wolves. For example, Final Fantasy 7’s Tifa Lockhart is coming to Street Fighter 6 next year, while Baki’s Yujiro Hanma is set to make a splash in Tekken 8 in 2027.
While these one-off characters aren’t ruffling too many feathers within the fighting game community (Tekken is a franchise known for including one or two oddball guests), the sheer amount of guest characters in CotW is raising eyebrows — especially given the fact that they don’t come from other fighting games.
“Lmfaoo, adding anything bruh. Kenshiro was dope, but what the f**k is this,” one player wrote on X.
“Funniest fighting game roster of all time bro,” another said.
“Love these two, but how did they get in over Baki, or hell, even Tokita Ohma?” another asked, referencing popular martial arts anime Kengan Ashura (which, funnily enough, celebrated a collaboration with Street Fighter 6 not long ago).
It’s worth noting that fighting games in general are no stranger to guest characters from totally different worlds; the Mortal Kombat franchise is perhaps the best example of this, having added characters like Robocop, Omni-Man, Homelander, the Terminator, Alien's Xenomorph, and many other similar fighters to its rosters over the years. However, the argument can be made that these additions followed a general theme in keeping with the Mortal Kombat vibe and universe, whereas City of the Wolves’ guests are all over the place (in fact, it’s the first time a real-life athlete has been put in a mainline fighting game — and what is Ronaldo doing in South Town, anyway?).
Whatever the case may be, SNK clearly sees a path forward with these guest characters, and I’m honestly intrigued where they’ll take the franchise next. Either way, the sheer amount of characters they’re adding to CotW per season is laudable… though not everyone is hyped for each fighter they’re putting out. (Speaking of which, can we get some more ladies on the roster?)

item.title: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve Brand Director Kazutoki Kono says developers spent so long working on Tasha that she ended up being the “most expensive character” in the entire game.
item.description:
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve brand director Kazutoki Kono joked that developers spent so long working on Tasha that she ended up being the “most expensive character” in the entire game.
Kono visited China for the first time to answer questions in a group interview with the media following a hands-on demo for the game, where he opened up about how popular Tasha has become over the last few months.
The pink-haired pilot is a fan favorite, and the game hasn’t even come out yet; set to release on October 2, oodles of future players are already obsessed with Tasha Severskaya, a former “star pilot in Yuktobania's acrobatic team, Zvezda.” Tasha hopped aboard the Endurance to capture publicity footage, but the ensuing war kept her on the vessel, and now she’s part of the Joker Flight squad.
Speaking with the media, Kono admitted that he was surprised by how popular Tasha had become on social media, revealing that he’s personally on “Team Kate Evans,” the Lieutenant Commander and leader of Queen Flight. He also revealed that Tasha took the longest to develop out of any other character in the game, since the team kept tweaking different aspects of her design to make sure they got her just right.
“Work on Tasha started relatively early, and she was originally designed by a different artist. She is also the character that took the longest to finalize. Her story and direction were already set, but we kept modifying various aspects afterward, making her the character we refined the longest during development. That's why inside the development team, we jokingly call her 'the most expensive character,'” he said, per Invenglobal.
As for why she’s so popular, Kono thinks it has to do with her fashion sense, saying her pink hair and outfits reflect trends that are currently popular among fans.
“I think elements like her personality, outfit, and especially her sense of fashion in wearing military attire so uniquely happened to fit current trends well, which contributed to all the attention she received,” he explained.
We got the chance to preview Ace Combat 8 this summer, with IGN’s Will Borger saying it was a "very grounded game" that left him “satisfied, but knowing [he] still had so much more to do.” He also got to speak with the devs about their ambitious plans for the game’s multiplayer, which will include 100-player lobbies, several different mission types, and a co-op warfare mode.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve releases on October 2, 2026 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC via Steam.
